cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Understand the Hurt
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge why their action hurt, not merely agree that it happened.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I saved you a front-row seat at my concert. Do you understand why it hurt? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I told you work might run late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I knew. I still looked at that empty seat before every song.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You needed someone there who knew what this meant to you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. You'd heard me practise for months. Please tell me you understand why someone else couldn't fill it.

mechanism: A directs a conversation about a missed concert, conceding the work dispute to retain B while seeking recognition of why B particular absence hurt.
confusable: Unlike demanding a generic apology for lateness, A needs B to understand the personal meaning of the reserved seat; borrowed authority narrows the discussion to keep B participating.
comparison: Knowledge of rehearsals and a saved seat differ from a practical dinner text misheard after job loss.
seedUse: Use D99-a concert/work/empty seat/rehearsals with S02-a limiting and rearranging discussion around B cooperation.
